Workplace rehabilitation standard

Human Resources Standard (QH-IMP-401-5)
Statement
This standard identifies the minimum requirements that evidence the implementation of the
Health, Safety and Wellbeing policy for managing injuries and illnesses related to active
workers compensation cases and all other workplace rehabilitation cases. This standard
supports recovery in the workplace and Queensland Health's commitment to ensuring and
improving the physical and psychological health, safety and wellbeing of workers.

Summary of this standard

e Commitment to improving wellbeing and rehabilitation outcomes for injured workers.

e Local processes detailed in rehabilitation procedure/s, including the 4 stages of
rehabilitation, identification of accountability area roles to fulfill key responsibilities for
workplace rehabilitation, a workers rights in relation to workplace rehabilitation and the
appropriate dispute resolution process to follow.

e Local workplace rehabilitation case management processes which meet legislative
requirements, inclusive of workers signed authorisation prior to exchanging confidential
information with third parties, a file for each worker undertaking workplace rehabilitation
containing copies of all documentation relevant to the injury and rehabilitation case, and
records storage and retention as stipulated by legislation.

e Availability of sufficient and appropriately qualified rehabilitation and return to work
coordinators (RRTWCs) to support injured workers through workplace rehabilitation, with
required RRTWC details submitted on an annual basis to WorkCover Queensland.

e A mandatory, current workers’ compensation insurance policy that covers all accountability
area workers, is held with WorkCover Queensland.

e Recognition of the health benefits of good work through stay at work and return to work
practices that support meaningful workplace rehabilitation plans, with rehabilitation goals
prioritised according to the return to work (RTW) hierarchy.

e Promotion of line manager responsibilities in workplace rehabilitation, including
identification of suitable duties and early and ongoing communication with workers.

Application

This standard applies to all accountability areas and includes employees within the

Department of Health (the department) and Hospital and Health Services (HHSs), in relation

to the provision of workplace rehabilitation for active workers compensation and all other

cases, including closed workers compensation claims, income protection and health

management. This document does not apply to the Queensland Ambulance Service and

instead, reference should be made to the relevant Queensland Ambulance Service

Requirements
1 Principles
Queensland Health is committed to providing workplace rehabilitation for injured/ill
workers, irrespective of the workers entitlement to compensation. Workplace rehabilitation
is the system for managing active workers compensation cases and all other cases to
support staff with injury and illness at work.
The primary goal of workplace rehabilitation shall be to support the injured/ill worker to
return to their substantive role within their usual work area, where reasonably practicable.
Queensland Health shall maintain an effective workplace rehabilitation system, in
accordance with the Workers’ Compensation and Rehabilitation Act 2003 (the act), which
meets the Guidelines for Standard for Rehabilitation, and/or other scheme directions as set
out in section 329A of the act.
Queensland Health is committed to preventing workplace psychosocial hazards as per the
requirements of Managing the Risks of Psychosocial Hazards at Work Code of Practice 2022. It
is recognised that psychosocial hazards may be associated with workplace rehabilitation,
and these can be mitigated by adopting a best practice workplace rehabilitation system.
The workplace rehabilitation system recognises and addresses potential psychosocial
hazards that may arise from changes experienced at certain stages of workplace
rehabilitation. These may include, but are not limited to, altered work hours or duties,
altered work environment and/or working relationships while undertaking suitable duties,
communication breakdown between key stakeholders, disagreement on suitable duties
tasks ora perceived lack of empathy, autonomy, fairness or control.
Queensland Health’s workplace rehabilitation system shall align with the principles outlined
in the Royal Australasian College of Physicians’ evidence-informed paper: It Pays to Care -
Bringing evidence-informed practice to work injury schemes helps workers and their
workplaces (April 2022). This national policy position promotes fair, constructive, and
supportive recovery journeys for injured and ill workers and is operationalised through local
rehabilitation processes and procedures.
Workplace rehabilitation processes shall embed a person-centred and trauma informed
approach to provide support for injured and ill workers in Queensland Health.
Queensland Health is committed to supporting a reframed relationship with Aboriginal
peoples and Torres Strait Islander peoples in accordance with Chapter 1 Part 3 of the Public
Sector Act 2022. Workplace rehabilitation will acknowledge unique experiences and cultural
needs of injured and ill workers for improved rehabilitation outcomes.
The workplace rehabilitation system shall encompass the rights and protections set out in
the Anti-Discrimination Act 1991 and the Human Rights Act 2019, to ensure that the principles
of freedom, respect, equality and dignity underpin workplace rehabilitation interactions and
actions and decisions occur in a way that is compatible with human rights.

A decision maker has an obligation under the Human Rights Act 2019 to act and make
decisions in a way that is compatible with human rights and give proper consideration to
human rights.

Queensland Health’s workplace rehabilitation system shall align with the vision and guiding

principles of the National Return to Work Strategy 2020-2030 and acknowledges the

influence that employers and workplaces have on rehabilitation outcomes.

The rehabilitation approach shall support the health and wellbeing benefits of good work, in

accordance with the principles outlined in the Royal Australasian College of Physicians’

position statement: Realising the health benefits of work.

2 Roles and Responsibilities

2A The employer / executive leader of the accountability area shall:

e Ensure the implementation of the health, safety and wellbeing policy in conjunction with
this standard and supporting documents within their accountability area.

e Ensure workers are insured, and remain insured, with WorkCover Queensland for all
work-related injuries and illnesses and not take action to avoid the workers
compensation process as per section 46A of the act.

e Ensure workers are aware of compensable entitlements for work-related injury/illness.

e Ensure sufficient and appropriately qualified rehabilitation and RRTWC are available to
support injured/ill workers through provision of workplace rehabilitation.

e Enable the implementation of suitable duties for all active workers compensation cases
and reasonable adjustment solutions, where reasonably practicable, with appropriate
allocation of resources and support, in accordance with section 228 of the act and the
Reasonable Adjustment HR Policy G3.

2.2 The line manager, or delegate, shall:

e Support the rehabilitation of injured/ill workers by ensuring the workplace
rehabilitation standard and local workplace rehabilitation procedures and processes are
followed.

e Ensure access to immediate first aid in the event of injury/illness occurring at work.

e Ensure all workplace incidents are recorded and investigated in accordance with the
requirements of local incident reporting procedures and Work Health and Safety Incident
response standard.

e Ensure that injured/ill workers are made aware of the workplace rehabilitation support
available, including availability of suitable duties and the required medical information
to consider reasonable adjustment, where applicable.

e Contact the injured/ill worker to offer workplace rehabilitation support and explain the
involvement of the RRTWC as soon as practicable after reporting of the injury/illness.

e Notify the workers designated RRTWC as soon as practicable, to facilitate a referral, as
required, to support workers with workplace rehabilitation and stay at work or return to
work processes.

e Maintain regular, transparent and timely communication, in the manner as agreed, with
the injured/ill worker throughout the rehabilitation process, whether at work or off work,

regarding the workers recovery and rehabilitation progress as well as communication of
any workplace changes and available supports.

e The immediate line manager is best placed to be the primary contact for the worker
wherever possible and facilitate the injured workers on-going connection with the
workplace.

e Where alternate work duties are required, identify and actively seek, with support from
the RRTWC if needed, meaningful suitable duties, and ensure suitable duties are made
available wherever reasonably practicable.

e Ensure suitable duties considerations are documented for all accepted workers
compensation cases. In rare instances, if it is determined that it is not practicable to
provide suitable duties to the worker, the evidence relied on to support that opinion
must be provided to the insurer, as per $228(2) of the act.

e Monitor implementation of the suitable duties program, to ensure duties provided
comply with the injured/ill workers current medical capacity, ensuring the health and
safety of the worker and others in the workplace.

e Provide the Payroll Injury and Rehabilitation Claims Team (PIARCT) with accurate
information pertaining to the injured/ill workers hours of work during the rehabilitation
process, via the approved form/s and within required payroll cut off schedule. Further
detail can be found at https://qheps.health.qld.gov.au/payroll-assistance/payroll-
services/piarct.

e Inform the worker of the appropriate dispute resolution process to follow in such cases
where the worker does not agree with elements of a proposed workplace rehabilitation
plan or suitable duties program.

e Ensure the rights of workers-on-workers compensation claims, are upheld, including
support to choose their treating medical practitioner and who is present during medical
treatment for the injury, as per s208B of the act.

2.3. The Rehabilitation and Return to Work Coordinator (RRTWC) shall:

e Support the rehabilitation of injured/ill workers by ensuring this Workplace
rehabilitation standard and local workplace rehabilitation procedures are followed.

e Ensure that an injured/ill worker who requires workplace rehabilitation for either a work
or non-work-related injury/illness, is contacted for workplace rehabilitation support, as
soon as practicable after notification of the injury/illness or request for support.

e Request the injured/ill workers signed authorisation to communicate with, and obtain
information from the workers treating doctor and/or other health practitioners, for the
purposes of planning and implementing workplace rehabilitation.

e Outline obligations of all parties under the act, where a workers compensation claim has
been made.

e Provide coordination of an injured/ill workers workplace rehabilitation and maintain
effective communication with key stakeholders in the workplace rehabilitation process.

e Review and provide input into rehabilitation and return to work plans for accepted
workers compensation claims, these must be provided by the insurer within 10 business
days of claim acceptance.

that will meet the injured/ill workers functional capacity to safely remain at, or return to

e Advise and support the line manager to identify meaningful suitable duties that comply

e Document all considerations, actions and decisions regarding suitable duties. Fora

e Inform the worker of the appropriate dispute resolution process to follow in such cases

e Ensure factual and timely case file notes are recorded for each workplace rehabilitation

e Ensure legislative compliance is maintained with respect to privacy, confidentiality and

e Ensure legislative compliance is maintained with respect to rehabilitation file records,

e Maintain and develop appropriate injury management skills and knowledge.

2.4 The injured/ill worker shall:

e Report a workplace incident in accordance with the requirements of local incident
reporting procedures and the Work health and safety Incident response standard.

e Notify the line manager of the emergence of injury/illness that may impact work
capacity, so that workplace rehabilitation support can be considered. This includes,
injury/illness and pre-existing medical conditions not covered by workers’
compensation.

e Notify the line manager of lodgement of a workers’ compensation claim application or
an income protection benefits claim application and submit a copy of the insurer-
approved medical certificate /capacity certificate.

e Ensure updated and current medical certificates are provided to the line manager and
RRTWC in a timely manner.

e Ensure appropriate leave application/s are submitted for accurate payments and to
prevent overpayments, which will result in an overpayment recovery process.

e Ensure medical certification remains current during participation in workplace
rehabilitation and any absence from the workplace, providing copies to the line manager
or agreed workplace contact.

— Should a medical certificate outlining commencement of work capacity not be
provided sufficiently in advance, the work unit, in consultation with the RRTWC or
other appropriate stakeholders, will need to determine if suitable duties can be
provided within the nominated timeframe.

e Make every effort to stay at work/return to work in accordance with medical capacity.

e Contribute constructively to RTW planning.

e Ensure duties performed on a suitable duties program comply with medical restrictions.

e Actively communicate with the RRTWC and line manager/other nominated workplace

e Engage in the overall workplace rehabilitation process, noting workers with active

2.5 The Payroll Injury and Rehab Claims Team (PIARCT) shall:

e Process all accepted workers compensation claim payment data and leave processing for
graduated return to work. Further detail can be found at
https://qheps.health.qld.gov.au/payroll-assistance/payroll-services/piarct.

3 Rights of key parties

Aworkers right to be informed of the workers’ compensation scheme available for work-

related injury and illness is recognised. Workers should be informed about their right to

make an application for compensation, choose their treating medical practitioner, who is
present during treatment, their workplace rehabilitation provider, consultation requirements
in development of rehabilitation and return to work plans, and the right to seek additional
advice and/or legal support, as needed.

Aworkers right to disagree with elements of a proposed workplace rehabilitation plan is

recognised, and the line manager/RRTWC shall inform the worker of the appropriate dispute

resolution process to follow.

e The commitment to continuing with workplace rehabilitation during and after the
dispute resolution process is recognised by both the worker and employer. This process
is outlined in the Individual employee grievances HR Policy E12.

The rights of all parties to request a review or appeal of a workers’ compensation or income

protection insurance claim decision is recognised and supported with a commitment to

continuing a workers rehabilitation program during and after any review or appeal process.

Refer to the respective insurer processes for further information.

4 Workplace rehabilitation system

4A Key principles

The four stages for managing the rehabilitation of workers with injury/illness in the

workplace are:

e Stage 1- immediate support and administrative processes

e Stage 2 - planning for stay at work or return to work

e Stage 3- implementing and supporting the plan

e Stage 4 - evaluating and reviewing rehabilitation outcomes.

The process flow for the workplace rehabilitation system, is outlined in attachment A.

The primary goal of workplace rehabilitation is to support the injured/ill worker to stay at

work throughout their recovery or return to performing their substantive role in their usual

work area, where reasonably practicable and no foreseeable risk to the worker or others

exists.

Suitable duties and/or temporary reasonable adjustment to the workplace (such as

modifications to work practices or duties) will be implemented for all active workers

compensation claims during the rehabilitation process, where it is indicated on a medical

certificate, reasonably practicable, and does not introduce unacceptable workplace risk. All

other cases will be supported on a case-by-case basis. Attachment B, suitable duties

workflow and the workplace rehabilitation guideline provide further detail.

Rehabilitation goals shall be prioritised according to the RTW hierarchy (see workplace

rehabilitation guideline) wherever feasible, whereby the RTW goal is identified with a

preference to returning the worker to their usual job in their usual work area. Where this is

not possible, processes as per the Reasonable adjustment HR policy G3 may be required.

4.2 Stage 1- Immediate support and administrative processes

4.21 First response

All injured /ill workers shall be offered immediate first aid in the event of injury/illness

occurring in the workplace. Access to first aid in the event of injury/illness, shall be

considered for workers working away from their usual workplace at the direction of the

employer.

More serious injury or illness may require activation of local emergency response

procedures, and support to access immediate medical care, as needed.

Workers requiring medical treatment for a work-related injury, which is not a medical

emergency, bodily fluid exposure or electric shock exposure, may access medical treatment

from a general practitioner, rather than an Emergency Department, where appropriate.

Immediate workplace supports may include:

e assistance to seek suitable medical care

e provision of information about availability of suitable duties

e safe transportation from work to medical care or place of residence, as applicable

e the injured workers line manager notifying next-of-kin, if applicable.

The workplace incident shall be recorded in Queensland Health’s incident management

system and in accordance with the requirements of local incident reporting procedures and

the work health and safety incident response standard. The workers line manager is

authorised to complete incident reporting on the workers behalf when a worker is unable to

do so.

When the line manager is made aware of injury/illness impacting a workers ability to

perform the genuine requirements of their role the worker should be offered rehabilitation

support and a request for supporting medical information may be required.

4.2.2 Workplace rehabilitation

Where medical certification supports stay at work or return to work, workplace rehabilitation

shall occur as per the workplace rehabilitation process outlined in attachment A. Further

guidance is available in the Workplace Rehabilitation Guideline.

A rehabilitation case file will be documented in the local case management system, for each

workers rehabilitation case.

4.2.3. Early Communication

Early and regular, ongoing communication with the injured worker from both the manager

(or nominated workplace contact) and RRTWC is vital to a successful rehabilitation outcome.

e Ongoing communication at agreed intervals, and method, between the injured/ill worker
and key stakeholders is a key principle underlying successful rehabilitation.

e Workers who do not receive ongoing meaningful contact may develop related secondary
injuries that can extend their workplace absence.

Early and ongoing communication with the treating doctor, following the workers signed

authorisation, ensures the doctor is aware of workplace support for rehabilitation and any

available suitable duties.

For accepted workers compensation claims, early and regular communication with the

insurer can inform the development of a rehabilitation and RTW plan.

4.2.4 Worker signed authority

Queensland Health holds a duty of care to workers and others in the workplace under the

Work Health and Safety Act 2011. Seeking medical information to assist a person to remain

safe in the workplace contributes to fulfilling this obligation.

The workers signed authority to obtain/release information relating to the medical

condition that is the subject of workplace rehabilitation, shall be obtained at the outset and

remain in place until the workers rehabilitation case has finalised or the worker advises
their employer, in writing, of their decision to revoke the authority.

Where authority is not provided by the worker, the RRTWC shall:

e Request relevant information for the purposes of planning and implementing workplace
rehabilitation from the workers’ compensation insurer for an accepted workers
compensation claim; and/or

e Communicate with treating practitioner/s via the injured/ill worker who obtains the
required medical information, in writing, from their treating practitioner/s.

4.2.5 Medical evidence

Medical evidence is relied upon to provide safe and effective workplace rehabilitation

support and ensure the accountability area’s duty of care for injured/ill workers and others

in the workplace is maintained.

A request for supporting information/ medical certification is required when workplace

rehabilitation is requested by a worker or their line manager.

Where a risk to the workers (or others’) health, safety or wellbeing is identified and/or when

there appears to have been a change to the workers capability to undertake the genuine

occupational requirements of their role, a request for supporting information regarding work

capacity may be made.

Where additional information is required in a stay at work/return-to-work process, the work

area, in consultation with the injured worker and the insurer, (as relevant), may seek to

engage an occupational rehabilitation provider (ORP). The ORP can conduct a worksite visit,
functional capacity assessment or occupational analysis and report, providing necessary
evidence and guidance on work capacity for a safe and sustainable stay at work/return to
work.

4.3 Stage 2 - Planning for stay at work/return to work

The purpose of planning workplace rehabilitation is to ensure a coordinated, safe and

sustainable process.

The principles and purpose of workplace rehabilitation apply to workers who stay at work

without a period of total incapacitation following injury/illness, but still require structured

and goal-oriented rehabilitation to regain functional capacity to return to pre-injury duties.

Workers with an accepted workers’ compensation claim, must be provided with

rehabilitation during the prescribed period as per s228 of the act, including the

accountability area taking all reasonable steps to assist or provide the worker with suitable
duties where reasonably practicable and supported by medical advice, as detailed in

attachment B.

4.3.1 Suitable duties program

If a worker cannot immediately undertake their pre-injury work duties, consideration shall

be given to the development of a temporary suitable duties program, as per the suitable

duties process flowchart at attachment B.

It is an expectation that meaningful suitable duties will be identified and made available

through the workers usual work unit, where reasonably practicable. If this is not practicable,

the line manager, in consultation with the RRTWC, may liaise with other managers in
different work units, to identify options, including consideration of host placement options.

If workers with accepted workers compensation claims cannot be offered suitable duties

consistent with medical restrictions, all actions and considerations of suitable duties must

be documented. This includes the steps taken or inquiries made to reach the determination,
this evidence is relied upon to support the opinion that it is not practicable to provide
suitable duties to the worker.

4.3.2 Temporary reasonable adjustment

If further clarification of any medical restrictions and associated temporary reasonable

adjustment is required, the RRTWC shall communicate with the treating health

practitioner/s, where the workers signed authority has been provided, or via the worker
directly.

e This can include requesting completion of physical and/or psychological work capability
checklist/s or requesting a medical report from treating medical practitioner/s, to clarify
work capacity and restrictions.

e Arequest for further medical information on work capacity, and temporary reasonable
adjustment/s, may be made at any stage during workplace rehabilitation.

To fulfil the duty of care Queensland Health accountability areas hold for workers, it is

necessary to seek information relevant to providing a safe place of work. Responding to

reasonable adjustment requests may be delayed where required information is not available
to make an informed decision about the adjustment requested. Reasonable adjustments
may include.

e Temporary modifications to the workplace.

e Time limited supernumerary arrangements to support stay at work/return to work.

e On-the-job training to support participation in temporary, alternate work duties.

e Temporary changes to work practices and roles.

Temporary reasonable adjustment may also include funding an ORP to undertake an

assessment and make recommendations for workplace rehabilitation, in accordance with the

Reasonable adjustment HR Policy G3.

4.3 Stage 3 - Implementing and managing the rehabilitation plan

4.3.1 Implement Stay at Work/RTW arrangements

The line manager shall monitor the workers progress and ensure they are coping with, and

complying with, the approved suitable duties.

e Concerns about the workers progress shall be immediately reported by the line manager
and/or worker to the RRTWC, who shall notify the treating doctor, with a view to
reviewing the program.

4.3.2 Review progress

As suitable duties programs are intended to be temporary and time limited, a cycle of

planning, implementing and reviewing shall regularly occur.

Timeframes for review are determined on a case-by-case basis and can be impacted by such

factors as progress, nature of injury, medical information provided and operational

requirements.

e Wherever possible, timeframes for review shall align with the workers injury type and
expected rate of recovery, facilitating a proactive review of their anticipated
rehabilitation progression.

4.3.3. Medical clearance certificate

Upon conclusion of participation in workplace rehabilitation a medical clearance certificate

should be obtained from the treating doctor, to confirm work capacity for full return to the

pre-injury (or other agreed) role.

A medical clearance certificate is used to document that a worker can safely return to their

pre-injury (or other agreed) role and is also helpful to ensure correct payment of wages as

the worker transitions to their pre-injury (or other agreed) working hours.

4.3.4 Rehabilitation case closure

Rehabilitation case closure shall be considered in such instances as:

a) The rehabilitation goal has been achieved, and a medical clearance certificate has been
received e.g. full return to pre-injury or other agreed role.

b) A mutually agreed return to work goal has been achieved e.g. hours/duties of pre-injury
role permanently modified through agreement by all parties.

c) Where the suitable duties program is not progressing e.g. hours/duties not increasing
towards pre-injury or another agreed role.

d) Where a safe and sustainable return to work cannot be achieved e.g. significant concerns
exist regarding the workers safety or their injury/ill health prevents an outcome for
return to work.

e) Where work incapacity arising from injury/illness persists, but no further workplace
rehabilitation involvement is medically indicated.

f) Where the worker is not actively participating in workplace rehabilitation.

In situations b) — f) outlined above, the rehabilitation case shall be closed and consultation

with the relevant Human Resources (HR) unit, rehabilitation contact and the responsible line

manager should occur, at which point relevant Department of Health HR policies, such as

Reasonable adjustment HR Policy G3, and/or Independent medical examinations of

employees HR Policy E11 should be considered.

4A Stage 4 - Evaluating and reviewing rehabilitation outcomes

The workplace rehabilitation system shall be subject to an ongoing evaluation and review

process.

4.4.1 Workplace rehabilitation outcome and feedback

The RRTWC shall advise all key stakeholders of workplace rehabilitation case closure and

document the outcome in the rehabilitation case file.

The RRTWC shall seek feedback at case closure from relevant stakeholders, including the

worker and line manager, via any of the following:

e case closure interview/s

e workplace rehabilitation evaluation survey

e other feedback method.

The RRTWC shall summarise and document the feedback derived from the case closure

interview, or other feedback methods, and include a copy of the feedback in the workers

rehabilitation case file.

The RRTWC shall obtain other relevant case closure documentation, including medical

clearance certificate, and record this in the workers rehabilitation case file.

4.4.2 Review outcomes

The RRTWC shall review rehabilitation outcomes and any stakeholder feedback received, to

identify any improvements, and ensure the workplace rehabilitation system is subject to

ongoing evaluation and review.

4.4.3. Records management and retention

The rehabilitation case file and all related records are to be retained for the stipulated

government retention and disposal timeframe (refer also to section 4.4.6).

4.4.4 Where a case transfers to Human Resources (HR) processes

Where work incapacity arising from injury illness persists and a safe and sustainable return

to work cannot be achieved through workplace rehabilitation, consultation with the line

manager, rehabilitation contact and HR team should occur so that application of relevant HR
policies may instead be considered by the appropriate delegate.

Transfer to the relevant HR unit will include appropriate case file summary and provision of

information relevant only to support the ongoing employment of the worker. Noting, except

for the purposes of rehabilitation, workers’ compensation documents must not be used or
obtained for decisions relating to the employment in accordance with s572A of the act.

4.4.5 Managing injury/illness without active workers compensation claim

Queensland Health is committed to the wellbeing of all staff and shall provide workplace

rehabilitation to workers with injuries/illnesses, that are not covered by an active workers’

compensation claim, where reasonably practicable.

Participation in the workplace rehabilitation process is voluntary for workers who have an

injury/illness that is not covered by an active workers compensation claim, except for some

compulsory processes.

Assistance shall be provided to workers where compulsory participation has been identified

through:

e A process managed under an income protection benefit scheme.

e A process managed by HR under the Public Sector Act 2022 arising from concerns that an
employee’s absence or unsatisfactory performance is caused by mental or physical
illness or disability.

When a line manager becomes aware that a worker is unfit to attend work due to

injury/illness, the line manager shall contact the worker to ascertain their medical capacity

and advise of the workplace rehabilitation process.

Where a worker with an injury/illness agrees to participate in a structured return to work

process, the line manager shall notify the RRTWC and the standard workplace rehabilitation

system shall be followed, as outlined in section 4.

Rehabilitation assistance can be provided to workers with non-work-related

injuries/illnesses where the following criteria is met:

e The worker has indicated their willingness to participate in a structured rehabilitation
and return to work process.

e The worker provides a current medical certificate endorsing a capacity for work anda
capacity to safely participate in a rehabilitation and return to work process.

e The worker provides a signed worker authorisation form permitting the RRTWC to
directly communicate with their treating doctor and other treating practitioner/s for the
purposes of coordinating rehabilitation and return to work. Alternatively, the worker may
advise the RRTWC to indirectly communicate with treating practitioners, via the worker
obtaining the required medical information, in writing, from their treating practitioner/s.

e The worker agrees to, and complies with, the elements of a suitable duties program as
developed by the RRTWC in conjunction with relevant stakeholders.

Where workers with injury/illness, not covered by an active workers compensation claim
decline to participate in a structured rehabilitation and return to work process, established
leave provisions as outlined in relevant HR policies will apply.

Those workers who decline to participate must provide current medical certificates whilst

accessing sick leave entitlements per Sick Leave HR Policy C64 and maintain communication,

at agreed intervals, with their line manager/ other nominated workplace contact during their
period of absence from work.

4.4.6 Confidentiality, use and retention of workplace rehabilitation and workers

compensation information

RRTWCs are required, in accordance with legislation and the code of conduct for the

Queensland public service, to ensure that information on the rehabilitation file is

appropriately obtained, used and stored.

A separate rehabilitation file shall be created and maintained for each worker undertaking

workplace rehabilitation and should contain copies of all relevant documentation, including

medical and allied health reports, correspondence, RTW plans, suitable duties programs,
case notes and related documents.

The rehabilitation file for each individual worker shall be stored in a secure environment

and managed in accordance with the Information Privacy Act 2009, Queensland Health’s

Information security policy, the act and relevant scheme directions.

e Electronic records of the workplace rehabilitation file can be retained in an electronic
document and records management system, in accordance with timeframes specified in
the Queensland Government's General Retention and Disposal Schedule (GRDS) for
